1. Card Migration & Transition Rules
​
Existing Card Phase-Out
: The old Swiggy HDFC Bank Credit Card is being phased out and cannot be retained. Once issued with consent, you cannot revert to the previous credit card.
Phased Rollout & Communication
: Upgrade communications are sent in phases. If you haven't received an offer, check your email/SMS/spam folders, verify if your card is blocked, or wait for upcoming phases.
Automatic Migration (If No Response)
: If you do not respond to the upgrade communication within the stipulated timeline, your card will automatically be migrated to the
Swiggy Ornge Card
. Customers who do not give explicit consent will receive a migration notice at least 30 days prior.
Using the Existing Card
: You can continue using your old card until the
earliest
of the following occurrences:
Making your first transaction on the upgraded card.
60 days
passing from the new card's issuance date.
The expiration date of your old card.
2. Card Details, Settings & Mandates
​
New Card Number
: The upgraded card will have a
different card number
.
Date of Upgrade
: Defined strictly as the
new card issuance date
(not the activation date).
Card Features & Controls
: Old card benefits become invalid upon upgrade. Security controls (transaction limits, international/online settings)
will not transfer
and must be reconfigured manually.
Autopay & Standing Instructions
: Existing autopay, e-mandates, and standing instructions
will not transfer automatically
; you must re-register them using the new card details.
3. Annual Fees & Renewal Cycle
​
The fee structure depends on whether your existing card is
Lifetime Free (LTF)
or
Paid ("prized")
:
If your current card is Lifetime Free (LTF)
:
Upgrading to Swiggy Ornge
: Remains
Lifetime Free (LTF)
.
Upgrading to Swiggy BLCK
: Annual fee of
₹1,000
applies.
If your current card is Paid ("Prized")
:
Upgrading to Swiggy Ornge
: Converts to
Lifetime Free (LTF)
.
Upgrading to Swiggy BLCK
: Offered as
First Year Free (FYF)
;
₹1,000/year
applies from the second year onward.
Fee Reset & Joining Fee
: The annual fee renewal cycle resets to the upgrade date, and joining fees (if applicable) will be charged within
120 days
of the upgrade.
4. Cashback & Transactions
​
Statement Visibility
: Transactions from the old card will appear in the upgraded card's statement.
Cashback Accrual
: Eligible transactions around and after the upgrade date earn cashback based on the new card’s rates and caps, credited on a
T+5 basis
(within 5 business days).
Query Period
: You can raise cashback queries regarding your old card for up to
1 month
from the new card's issuance date.
5. Card Delivery & Swiggy App Updates
​
Physical Delivery
: The card is dispatched to your bank-registered address within
7–10 working days
. If non-delivery occurs, contact HDFC Bank Customer Care or update your address via the bank’s official online link to request branch redirection or re-dispatch.
Swiggy App Reflection
: The new card will display in the Swiggy App within
20 days
of the upgrade.
6. Welcome Benefits & Membership Rules
​
Welcome Benefit Coupon
: Provided as a coupon code via SMS/email/notifications within
20 days
of activating the upgraded card. The coupon is valid for
1 year
from the card issuance date.
Applicable Memberships
:
Swiggy Ornge Card
: Unlocks
1 year of Swiggy One membership
.
Swiggy BLCK Card
: Unlocks
3 months of Swiggy BLCK membership
.
Handling Existing Memberships Upon Coupon Redemption
:
Upgrading to Ornge with active BLCK
: BLCK is cancelled, and a pro-rata refund is issued for the remaining duration.
Upgrading to Ornge with active Swiggy One
: Swiggy One validity is extended.
Upgrading to BLCK with active BLCK
: BLCK validity is extended.
Upgrading to BLCK with active Swiggy One
: Swiggy One is cancelled, and a pro-rata refund is issued for the remaining duration.

How did you managed to apply rwc50 after conversion?
Offline via form or phone bankin or via RM or any other channel?

So I will lay out the whole process here:
My father has HDFC bank account since a long time back (around 2001). He worked for a very big PSU and hence was considered a govt employee and had a salary account with HDFC. He retired a few years ago and since then his account was converted into a general savings account. Our whole family is in a Imperia Family Group. As soon as I learnt about RWC50 (June 2026) I tried applying the same via online channels but was unsuccessful. A new HDFC branch recently opened near our home and the branch manager of that new branch met my father in our old branch and told him that this new branch is closer to our home and we can also get a free locker under Imperia programme (which we knew already but didn't take because the old branch was far from our home). Hence my father shifted our branch to the new branch and because it is new branch, not many people know about it and it remains empty and hence we get VIP like treatment because we can just walk in and there's no rush or anything.
As my father now opened a locker there so he visits it regularly and I told him to fill out the physical form and apply for RWC50. When he tried to apply the same the branch official told him his account needs to be converted into a senior citizen account variant only then he will be able to apply for the RWC50 card. We told her to go ahead with the conversion, but since it was also a joint account with my mother, it needed both holder's signatures. Which took us a few more days as my mother doesn't usually visit the branch. After the signatures was done on his next visit with my mother, it took a couple of days for the conversion process. He applied the card on this next visit to the branch(I mentioned specifically RWC50 to the branch employee over the call) and after that the card appeared in netbanking within the same day but we needed to wait for the physical delivery for activation which took 3-5 days.
TLDR: Offline via form

the.trio.verseity.438 said:
For those who don't know about the HDFC Classic Banking Program, it's a scheme for HDFC account holders belonging to the same family, where if any one member maintains Rs. 1 Lakh or more in their HDFC savings account, the rest of the family members can use their accounts without any MAB requirement — basically as a zero-balance account.
Before going further — we're a 4-member family, and out of us, only I currently hold a savings account with HDFC. Because of the good behavior of the bank employees and dedicated RM support, I once mentioned to my RM that I'd like to open savings accounts for the rest of my family members there too. Since then, the RM has consistently suggested we opt for the Classic Banking Program. As my father is planning to park 1-2L somewhere for emergencies, the HDFC Classic Banking Program looks like a perfect fit for us, since it would let the rest of the family enjoy zero-balance savings accounts with HDFC.
The RM is suggesting we first open 25K MAB savings accounts for the rest of my family, and then enroll us in the Classic Banking Program afterward.
We mostly agree with her, except on one point — the variant of the savings account.
According to her, if we opt for the 25K MAB account, we'll get the LTF HDFC Platinum debit card with unlimited free ATM transactions, whereas with the 10K MAB account, we'd get the Moneyback debit card with a Rs. 500 annual charge and only the first 5 ATM transactions free. Under the Classic Banking Program, there'd be no need to maintain that 25K MAB in these accounts, so they'd effectively become zero-balance accounts.
Now my concern is this — my father is keeping that fund purely for emergencies. He initially planned to put it in an FD, but with the Classic Banking Program, he'd need to maintain a minimum balance of 1L in his account at all times. In the future, if an emergency arises and we use up this fund without having enough uninvested money to put back into his account, then all my family members would each have to maintain 25K in their individual HDFC savings accounts — totaling Rs. 1L anyway. That could be difficult, since they'd have been using these as zero-balance accounts up to that point, and would then suddenly need to maintain at least a 25K MAB.
That's why I'm making this post to collect your suggestions on this.
What should I do —
go with the 10K MAB account or,
go with the 25K MAB account or,
Completely stay out of this Classic Banking Program
Edit — As of now, my main question is whether there's any real-life advantage of the 25K MAB account over the 10K MAB account. If there are enough good advantages with that variant, we might choose it over the 10K MAB account.

text: I had an extremely disappointing and frustrating experience at the HDFC Bank Durgapuri Branch. I regularly visit the branch to deposit money on behalf of the company I work for. During my recent visit, there was only one person ahead of me in the deposit queue, yet I had to wait approximately 15–20 minutes before my turn because the customer care executive, Ms. Sonali Bhadouriya, was taking an unusually long time to process the previous customer. When my turn came, I handed over the cash amounting to ₹1,07,340 along with the properly completed deposit slip. The cash was counted by the executive, the slip was stamped, and I was allowed to leave the counter, giving me the clear impression that the transaction had been completed. However, just 3–4 minutes after leaving the branch, I received a call asking me to return immediately. I had to leave my work and come back to the branch, only to be told that one ₹500 note supposedly could not be accepted. I questioned why this had not been communicated before I was allowed to leave and why the deposit slip had already been stamped and the transaction treated as completed. During the discussion, my original deposit slip was taken and torn, and I was asked to fill out a new slip showing one less note. I was then given a ₹500 note back, which had a black mark on it. While I was filling out the new slip, the executive again asked for the returned note and consulted a senior, who confirmed that the note could be accepted. However, the executive then exchanged that note for another ₹500 note and claimed that the second note was actually mine. Since this was a different note from the one that had just been returned to me, I was understandably uncomfortable accepting it without proper verification. I requested that the CCTV footage be checked to establish exactly what had happened. I was then asked to wait and was eventually told to return at 3:30 PM for the CCTV verification. By that point, approximately one hour of my working time had already been wasted due to this entire situation. I understand that banks have procedures for handling questionable currency notes, but the way this matter was handled was extremely inconvenient and left me feeling that my time and concerns were not being taken seriously. I request HDFC Bank management to investigate this incident, review the relevant CCTV footage and transaction records, and take appropriate action if any procedural lapse or misconduct is found. Customers should not have to repeatedly leave their workplace, wait unnecessarily, or deal with confusion regarding their cash and deposit records because of avoidable errors at the counter. I hope the branch takes this feedback seriously and ensures that such an experience does not happen to other customers in the future.

text: HDFC Home Loan Branch Jayanagar/Bengaluru: I was sold an insurance policy to cover my big home loan. I was not informed of the whole procedure as to how HDFC bank works with HDFC Ergo. I was told that the insurance policy can be cancelled anytime I think that the residual risk is low. However, after 2 years when I wanted to cancel, they dragged it for months, not giving a proper reason. Then when I persistently kept asking them to close it no matter what, they did so without properly giving me the details about the residual loan amount, how much it would cost me, what would be beneficial from my (customer) perspective. Turns out, I had to pay a huge sum, as an insurance "loan" (called Insurance Premium Funding) was taken from HDFC bank to finance the policy. Policy was cancelled, however I still had to either pay the EMI for that loan or settle it completely. Turns out, it would have been cheaper for me to have continued with the policy, as the remaining loan amount was more or less equal to that of my monthly payments x no. of payments. I simply lost the insurance cover while having paid the full amount including interest etc.
title: Horrible service and zero transparency

Yes, I agree with your concern because the majority of these banks aim to attract new customers by providing freebies only if you maintain a high TRV/NRV. However, in the end, the bank makes more profits than the customer. Additionally, banks have the complete power to alter the terms and conditions of any particular program, and since customers are obligated to pay the full cost of their so-called T&C, it is up to them to decide whether or not to continue doing business with the bank. I really wish I had the choice to switch banks freely if one isn't serving me well.
Even though my hometown and work town fall into Tier 2 and Tier 1 respectively, there still aren't too many bank options. Aside from PSU banks (even the less common ones like CBOI, UCO, IOB, BOM, IB), there's mainly HDFC, ICICI, Axis, IDBI, and two or three NBFCs and SFBs. Well-performing banks like IDFC, and one of the top private banks, Kotak, don't have a single branch within a 500 KM radius.
Now, coming to the available options — PSU banks mostly have horrible experiences; you can't expect any helpful behavior from the staff, and everything has to be sorted out by yourself.
Among the private options:
Axis is infamous for scamming its customers, so I can't enroll my whole family with a bank like that.
ICICI is smoking something high — neither the employees nor the official site clearly mention how many types of savings accounts ICICI actually offers, unlike HDFC, which clearly lists its 10K and 25K account variants. The employees are mostly focused on pushing the 3-in-1 account program, which isn't suitable for everyone.
So the last option left is HDFC. I haven't had any bad experience with them so far, so I've decided to enroll my family there. If this bank ever betrays us, well, we won't have any option to switch — either continue with them or give up on them completely.

text: I was sold an insurance policy to cover my big home loan. I was not informed of the whole procedure as to how HDFC bank works with HDFC Ergo. I was told that the insurance policy can be cancelled anytime I think that the residual risk is low. However, after 2 years when I wanted to cancel, they dragged it for months, not giving a proper reason. Then when I persistently kept asking them to close it no matter what, they did so without properly giving me the details about the residual loan amount, how much it would cost me, what would be beneficial from my(customer) perspective. Turns out, I had to pay a huge sum, as an insurance "loan"(called Insurance Premium Funding) was taken from HDFC bank to finance the policy. Policy was cancelled, however I still had to either pay the EMI for that loan or settle it completely. Turns out, it would have been cheaper for me to have continued with the policy, as the remaining loan amount was more or less equal to that of my monthly payments x no. of payments. I simply lost the insurance cover while having paid the full amount including interest etc.

title: No need of HDFC MAB for Savings Max?

text:
For those who don't know about the HDFC Classic Banking Program, it's a scheme for HDFC account holders belonging to the same family, where if any one member maintains Rs. 1 Lakh or more in their HDFC savings account, the rest of the family members can use their accounts without any MAB requirement — basically as a zero-balance account.
Before going further — we're a 4-member family, and out of us, only I currently hold a savings account with HDFC. Because of the good behavior of the bank employees and dedicated RM support, I once mentioned to my RM that I'd like to open savings accounts for the rest of my family members there too. Since then, the RM has consistently suggested we opt for the Classic Banking Program. As my father is planning to park 1-2L somewhere for emergencies, the HDFC Classic Banking Program looks like a perfect fit for us, since it would let the rest of the family enjoy zero-balance savings accounts with HDFC.
The RM is suggesting we first open 25K MAB savings accounts for the rest of my family, and then enroll us in the Classic Banking Program afterward.
We mostly agree with her, except on one point — the variant of the savings account.
According to her, if we opt for the 25K MAB account, we'll get the LTF HDFC Platinum debit card with unlimited free ATM transactions, whereas with the 10K MAB account, we'd get the Moneyback debit card with a Rs. 500 annual charge and only the first 5 ATM transactions free. Under the Classic Banking Program, there'd be no need to maintain that 25K MAB in these accounts, so they'd effectively become zero-balance accounts.
Now my concern is this — my father is keeping that fund purely for emergencies. He initially planned to put it in an FD, but with the Classic Banking Program, he'd need to maintain a minimum balance of 1L in his account at all times. In the future, if an emergency arises and we use up this fund without having enough uninvested money to put back into his account, then all my family members would each have to maintain 25K in their individual HDFC savings accounts — totaling Rs. 1L anyway. That could be difficult, since they'd have been using these as zero-balance accounts up to that point, and would then suddenly need to maintain at least a 25K MAB.
That's why I'm making this post to collect your suggestions on this.
What should I do —
go with the 10K MAB account or,
go with the 25K MAB account or,
Completely stay out of this Classic Banking Program
Edit — As of now, my main question is whether there's any real-life advantage of the 25K MAB account over the 10K MAB account. If there are enough good advantages with that variant, we might choose it over the 10K MAB account.
title: HDFC Classic Banking Program — RM is suggesting opening 25K MAB accounts instead of 10K MAB

I had opened an HDFC Bank account at the Whitefield Branch, Bangalore – 560066. I used the account regularly for around 3–4 months. After that, although there was sufficient balance in my account, the bank temporarily blocked my account.
I personally visited the branch to resolve the issue. The bank asked me to provide my long/permanent address and additional KYC documents. I submitted my original PAN Card, Voter ID, Aadhaar Card and all other required documents. However, the bank continued to raise issues regarding my permanent address.
Later, I returned to my hometown in Kolkata and completed the required home verification for my HDFC Bank account. After the verification was completed, my account started working normally again.
After that, HDFC Bank offered me a credit card, which I accepted. However, I never generated or used the PIN for the credit card. I still have the SMS records related to the transaction/amount of approximately ₹40,000.
When I contacted the bank regarding this issue, I was told to contact Customer Care and report the matter to Cyber Crime. Accordingly, I filed a Cyber Crime complaint and also sent more than 100 emails to HDFC Bank regarding the matter. I submitted dispute forms and all the necessary information and documents requested by the bank.
In addition to this, HDFC Bank has placed a hold/lien of approximately ₹20,000 on my account. I have repeatedly contacted the bank and submitted my Debit Card, Credit Card and Passbook to the bank. Despite this, almost two years have passed, and my issue has still not been resolved.
Even though I have already surrendered the cards and passbook and repeatedly requested the bank to resolve and close the matter, I continue to receive monthly maintenance charges and SMS notifications from HDFC Bank.
This entire experience has caused me significant mental stress, inconvenience and financial loss. Despite repeated complaints, emails, dispute forms and visits to the bank, I have not received a proper resolution even after almost two years.
Based on my experience, I am extremely disappointed with the way HDFC Bank has handled my case. I feel that the bank has failed to provide proper customer service and a satisfactory resolution to my genuine complaint.
I request the concerned authority to urgently investigate my case, remove any wrongful hold/lien or charges, stop further unnecessary charges and SMS notifications, resolve the disputed transaction, and provide me with a written explanation and final resolution.my personal experience hdfc bank are froud bank in under india

text:
A side effect of Technofino in Inquiries (8 in 6 months (6 in 3 months), 2 due to expire on 6th sep and 24th sep, 24th is HDFC, checked cards last time and backed out)
An update to the axis experience, if you have not read that one, check it out for context on my profile. Figured since I was already documenting data points I might as well add one more. This is a fresh data point following that post.
Applied for HDFC BizGrow Visa about an hour ago (not preapproved, fresh application). Started at 5.24PM, after filling basic details (address was prefilled from bank records), CRIF and Cibil were checked for eligibility after which cards were shown (weird since last time - March, they only checked cibil) after proceeding with Bizgrow visa from the list, was supposed to fill more data then app verification (netbank, aadhar or debit card) and it said application submitted with a reference number but no vkyc link or any mention of it, thought this will be rejected for sure because HDFC is conservative with inquiries but after 8 minutes of submitting the application at 5.27PM, I received a text and email at 5.35PM (text mentioned application successful, which to me meant rejection just that the process was successful, email mentioned card approved will be delivered in 3-5 days)
Profile at time of application (1st September 2026)
CIBIL: 779
Utilisation - 10%
Total visible credit: 7.34L (ICICI APay 3.3L, ICICI MMT 3.3L, IDFC Ashva 74K)
Active inquiries in 6 months: 8 including this HDFC pull (20th lifetime, no more planned, no relevant issuers left)
ITR AY 2026-27: 10,74,310 (Income proof was not asked, or even asked to fill the amount at all)
Employment: Self employed
Existing HDFC relationship: Savings account, previously held HDFC MB+ with total spend of approximately 5.42L (first card, from March 2024-March 2026), closed cleanly with zero dues (Because no le was given even after providing all proof and a solid credit profile at the time, card had 50k limit lowest at the time)
Application Process
Applied online. Income documents not requested. Only application verification was required (through netbank/aadhar/debit card) no vKYC, no physical verification. Both CRIF and CIBIL were pulled.
Approved in 8 minutes flat. Card going to be dispatched, arriving in 3 to 5 days.
Assumption
HDFC probably weighted both the existing savings account relationship and previous card spend history heavily. The instant approval with no income verification and no vKYC strongly suggests the decision was based on internal ETB data, I don't use the savings account at all, it just has MAB left, my main is IDFC for now ever since I closed the HDFC card (Heavy deposits, planning to diversify to both HDFC and IDFC equally)
Limit - unknown for now. (Hoping a good amount is given and not base, but even if that is the case, I will be keeping it even if in my drawer because HDFC does give unpredictable LE, data points predict.
title: HDFC BizGrow Approved in 8 Minutes | ETB

text:
❌ Extremely Disappointing HDFC Credit Card Experience – Unclear Finance Charges & Poor Resolution

I am extremely disappointed with my experience with HDFC Bank’s credit card.

My main concern is not simply that charges were applied, but the lack of clear explanation and transparency regarding finance charges and the way the outstanding amount was calculated

1. Finance Charges – No Clear Explanation

I made substantial payments towards my credit card outstanding, yet finance charges were still applied. What is particularly frustrating is that I could not get a clear, simple explanation of exactly how these charges were calculated, for which period, and on what amount.

As a customer, I should be able to understand every charge appearing on my statement without having to repeatedly contact customer support.

 2. Charges Keep Adding Up

Credit card statements already contain multiple components such as outstanding amounts, finance charges, GST and other applicable fees. When these are not explained properly, it becomes extremely difficult for an ordinary customer to understand the actual liability.

I strongly believe that banks should provide a clear calculation/breakdown of every finance charge, rather than simply displaying an amount in the statement.

 3. Customer Support Needs Major Improvement

My experience with customer support has also been disappointing. Instead of receiving a straightforward calculation and resolution, customers often have to go through multiple interactions and complaints.

If a customer questions a charge, the bank should explain:

* What transaction triggered the charge?
* What amount was considered for calculation?
* What dates were considered?
* What rate was applied?
* How was GST calculated?
* Why was the final amount charged?

A simple and transparent calculation would resolve most of these concerns.

I am not against legitimate credit-card charges. If a charge is genuinely applicable under the card's terms and conditions, the bank should clearly explain it.

My concern is the lack of transparency, complicated calculations and difficulty in getting a satisfactory explanation.

After this experience, I would strongly recommend that anyone considering an HDFC credit card carefully understand the finance-charge mechanism, applicable fees and payment conditions before using it.

Very disappointing experience. I expected much better transparency and customer service from HDFC Bank.

sovon said:
Thought of sharing my experience with HDFC. Me and my brother opened HDFC Regular savings accounts with 10k Average minimum balance, on the same day, but the way things unfolded was surprisingly different.
We both opened regular savings accounts (Insta Kit) on 20th August 2025. Accounts were activated within 24 hours. We funded ₹50,000 each initially and received the Millennia debit card instantly.
For the first few months, both of us maintained around ₹1.5L balance till October. Later it reduced to around ₹1L, and from January 2026 it has been floating between ₹50k–₹80k. On paper, both accounts looked almost identical.
My usage was retail heavy. I routed most of my daily expenses through HDFC, used the debit card actively and even completed the ₹40k Millennia milestone.
My brother barely did retail spends. Most of his activity was through Groww and Zerodha after shifting from SBI. Interestingly, he even started receiving HDFC mutual fund related marketing emails, which I never received.
On 12th January, my brother received a pre-approved offer via email and SMS. He applied the same day.
Instant approval.
No CIBIL enquiry.
No CRIF enquiry.
No verification calls.
He was offered
:
MoneyBack+ Visa LTF
Swiggy (paid)
Indian Oil (paid)
He chose MoneyBack+ LTF with ₹76,000 limit.
For context, he has:
3 years credit history
CIBIL 779
Only 2 previous hard enquiries
Supermoney Utkarsh FD card with 5k limit.
Axis card with ₹37k limit
It genuinely looked like pure internal relationship-based approval.
He was offered a 2.75L Two wheeler loan from HDFC few days before this pre approved credit card offer.
Meanwhile – I Was Waiting
From December onwards, I was only getting the generic Pixel card mails.
No real pre-approved offer.
On January 2026, I also got a pre-approved 2.5L Two wheeler loan.
On 10th February exactly after his window closed, on 10th February I received my pre-approved email, SMS and WhatsApp.
Through Xpressway it showed all paid cards.
Through the SMS link I could see:
MoneyBack+ LTF
Indian Oil LTF
Swiggy (paid)
I selected MoneyBack+.
Then came the panic moment.
On my first attempt I got a system error:
“
Your request could not be processed
.”
Immediately received CRIF hard enquiry SMS.
At that point, I genuinely thought it was over.
Since the enquiry had already happened, I tried again. Second attempt went through and application was submitted around 2 PM.
But unlike my brother:
Mine didn’t get instant approval
Status went into pending
Around 4 PM, CIBIL hard enquiry happened
Next day, 11th February around 11 AM, approval SMS finally came.
On 12th February, card appeared in MyCards with ₹72,000 limit.
Then over the next 24–48 hours it reflected in PayZapp and NetBanking.
Some interesting incident happened with My Brother :
On 12th February, exactly one month after his first approval, my brother applied for HDFC Swiggy card via Swiggy app.
This time:
A. CRIF enquiry
B. CIBIL enquiry
C. Estimated limit ₹76k (floater with existing card)
Approved instantly.
Next day visible in MyCards with temporary ₹5k limit (to be updated to ₹76k).
So even after our account age same, HDFC put us on different batches.
Higher retail transaction volume did not guarantee earlier offer.
Investment routing might be weighted differently in their internal algorithm.
Still happy to finally enter HDFC ecosystem. This is my first HDFC unsecured card despite 5 years of history.
Update: 16/02/2026
Just got my Hdfc Money Back+ delivered, completed the pin set up.
Somehow I became greedy and applied for the LTF Swiggy Credit Card from Swiggy app.
CRIF + CIBIL Hard enquiry happened, and then verified by ATM pin, got application submission mail + sms. Within 1 minute recieved the Credit Card approval sms.
So within a week a got 2 HDFC credit card approved.
Final update: 21st February 2026
Got my Swiggy Card delivered. Form the Swiggy app got 3 month Swiggy membership, additional 9 months will be added later.

cardio_guy said:
HDFC, Axis and HSBC are becoming three of the most interesting credit-card ecosystems in India, but they are taking very different approaches. HDFC has built a huge ecosystem around cards, SmartBuy, vouchers, UPI and co-branded products. Axis has built one of India's strongest miles and premium-card ecosystems around EDGE Miles and Travel EDGE. HSBC has a smaller portfolio, but is increasingly interesting because of its transferable travel currency, 1:1 airline/hotel transfers and Travel with Points platform powered by Hopper. So instead of asking which individual card is best, I wanted to compare the entire ecosystem — cards, reward currencies, transfer partners, accelerated platforms, cashback, co-brands, milestones and banking relationships.

HDFC's strength is the sheer depth of its ecosystem. It has cards covering cashback, UPI, travel, vouchers, hotels, shopping and premium rewards, with SmartBuy sitting above the cards as an accelerated rewards platform. Axis has a similarly broad portfolio, but its premium proposition is more heavily tilted towards miles and travel. HSBC has fewer cards, but its current lineup is much more focused: TravelOne, Premier, Live+, Taj and a few entry-level products.

HDFC has the cleanest premium ladder. Regalia Gold sits in the mass-premium segment, DCB Metal moves into serious rewards optimisation, and Infinia is the flagship. The big advantage is that HDFC's premium cards work particularly well with SmartBuy, where selected travel, shopping and voucher transactions can earn accelerated rewards. SmartBuy is therefore a major part of the HDFC proposition rather than simply an additional booking portal.
Axis has a much more complicated premium structure. Atlas, Horizon, Magnus, Olympus, Reserve and Primus are not simply successive versions of the same card; each has a different use case. Atlas is especially interesting because it combines normal spending, travel accelerators, milestone rewards and a dedicated miles-transfer programme. Current Atlas benefits include 2 EDGE Miles/₹100 on base spending and 5 EDGE Miles/₹100 on eligible direct airline, hotel and Travel EDGE spending, with ₹7.5 lakh and ₹15 lakh milestones driving Gold and Platinum tiers.
HSBC is much simpler. TravelOne is the main travel-focused card, while Premier is tied to the HSBC Premier banking relationship. TravelOne currently earns 2 points/₹100 on general spending and 4 points/₹100 on flights, travel aggregators and foreign-currency transactions. It also gives 10,000 bonus points after ₹12 lakh annual spending.

This is where Axis and HSBC become particularly interesting. Atlas EDGE Miles can be transferred to partner programmes at 1 EDGE Mile = 2 partner miles, while HSBC TravelOne points currently transfer 1:1 to a wide range of airline and hotel programmes. HSBC's current partner list includes Singapore Airlines KrisFlyer, Air India Maharaja Club, British Airways, Qatar, Qantas and others; hotel partners include Accor ALL, Marriott Bonvoy, IHG, Shangri-La and Wyndham.
HDFC's approach is different. Its reward currency becomes much more powerful when combined with SmartBuy and card-specific redemption options. This means the headline base reward rate doesn't tell the full story. For someone willing to optimise,
HDFC is often about how you earn; Axis and HSBC are increasingly about where you can move the points.

It has cards covering cashback, UPI, travel, vouchers, hotels, shopping and premium rewards, with SmartBuy sitting above the cards as an accelerated rewards platform. Axis has a similarly broad portfolio, but its premium proposition is more heavily tilted towards miles and travel. HDFC has the cleanest premium ladder. Regalia Gold sits in the mass-premium segment, DCB Metal moves into serious rewards optimisation, and Infinia is the flagship. Axis has a much more complicated premium structure. Atlas, Horizon, Magnus, Olympus, Reserve and Primus are not simply successive versions of the same card; each has a different use case. Atlas is especially interesting because it combines normal spending, travel accelerators, milestone rewards and a dedicated miles-transfer programme. Current Atlas benefits include 2 EDGE Miles/₹100 on base spending and 5 EDGE Miles/₹100 on eligible direct airline, hotel and Travel EDGE spending, with ₹7.5 lakh and ₹15 lakh milestones driving Gold and Platinum tiers.
HSBC is much simpler. TravelOne is the main travel-focused card, while Premier is tied to the HSBC Premier banking relationship. TravelOne currently earns 2 points/₹100 on general spending and 4 points/₹100 on flights, travel aggregators and foreign-currency transactions. It also gives 10,000 bonus points after ₹12 lakh annual spending.

Dear Sir/ Madam,
I have an NRE+NRO account in HDFC, Bettiah Branch, Bihar. I have always maintained the minimum balance and had a very good transaction record. Due to a financial crisis in the years 2024-25, I could not maintain the minimum balance for a couple of months. I approached the bank and asked to revoke the non-maintenance fine imposed, which is not mandatory under the RBI guidelines.
They, the HDFC officials, through their official email channels, agreed and assured me of waiving off all the dues and encouraged me to use the account, starting with depositing the minimum balance. I deposited Rs 24.000 agianst Rs 20, 000 minimum balance for the two accounts, NRE and NRO (Rs. 10, 000 for each). They deducted all my money, showing a negative otstanding fine/ balance, which is against RBI guidelines.
I informed them about the same regarding the unfair deduction, and they kept on torturing me in the name of looking into the matter. They finally agreed to return the money but returned only 3540 and started deducting the minimum balance fine from the same day. Seeing that there is a misunderstanding, I withdrew the remaining amount of Rs. 7, 363.14. I reported the same to the executive through the same channel. They assured me that they would resolve the issue, but it never happened. They returned Rs. 3540 again into my account and started deducting minimum balance fines from the same amount. In the meantime, I was in correspondence with the customer care team on Social Media, where they finally refused to return the money deducted unfairly. After seeing these months of deceit, torture, and disappointment, I reported the matter to INGRAM (Jaago Grahak Jaago). The bank lied on the platform, saying that I am again and again seeking a free refund and closed the matter from their end. I was suggested to move to this "ConsumerComplaints" platform if the resolution was not done.
